---
name: A household it reads wrongly
about: Stillwatch called a day something it was not
title: ''
labels: judgement
assignees: ''
---

**What the day actually was**

Somebody left, somebody stopped, somebody had a visitor, two people were home,
a camera was failing. Whatever was really going on.

**What Stillwatch said**

The state, and the sentence it gave underneath. The sentence matters more than
the state, because it says which part of the reasoning went wrong.

**When**

The time of day, and roughly how long the quiet had lasted.

**The events, if you have them**

A few lines of the stream, or the scenario and seed if this came from the
simulator. Timestamps, device names and whether each camera is at a way out or
inside the home.

**What it should have said**

Including the reason, if you can put it in a sentence. That is usually the
thing worth arguing about.
